newsitem.title: UK: Treasuries drift higher in London, auction ahead.
newsitem.headline: Treasuries drift higher in London, auction ahead.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries popped higher in London on Thursday but trade remained thin ahead of a five-year note auction and a stream of data beginning on Friday, traders said.
News that Moody's Investor Service said debt of the U.S. was still solidly Aaa came out of the blue for the market but was largely overlooked, they said.
"It's very quiet," said a trader at a U.S. bank in London. "We're just drifting up."
The benchmark long bond was quoted at 95-04 at 1034 GMT, up from a close of 94.30 in Tokyo and 94.31 in New York on Wednesday.
Upheaval in European markets after the Bundesbank rejected Germany's plans to revalue its gold assets to help get it into single currency union, gave Treasuries a bit of a spin, they said.
"There is an increasing bias to owning U.S. versus Europe as EMU looks more uncertain," the trader at the U.S. bank said.

But the market was expected to have difficulty with a five-year note sale later, after a mediocre sale of two-year notes on Wednesday. The Treasury was set to auction $12.0 billion of five-years at 1745 GMT.
"Obviously the two-year note was not especially good and we'll probably struggle with the five-year," George Magnus, chief international economist at UBS in London, said.
Data this session included weekly jobless claims, the New York Association of Purchasing Managers report for May and weekly money supply data.
But Treasuries would likely be on hold until revised GDP data and the Chicago Purchasing Mangers Index on Friday. Next week comes key payroll data.
"The impact of the April slowdown is pretty much over now and I am expecting the market to drift to the soft side," Magnus said.

Moody's said in its first in-depth credit report on the United States there were concerns related primarily to the country's hefty upcoming medical and pension costs associated with an aging population.
But these were outweighed by the size and depth of the U.S. economy.
In the futures market, the June T-bond contract was quoted at 108-28, up 5/32 from the Chicago pit settlement.
